To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the presence of an extensive intraductal (EIC+) component and young age were the only significant factors associated with the risk breast recurrence for patients with early breast cancer treated with conservative surgery (CS), followed by radiation therapy (RT).

the presence of an extensive intraductal (EIC+) component in the breast cancer and very young age (34 years or less) are significant risk factors for breast recurrence following treatment with conservative surgery and radiotherapy.

(1) the presence of an EIC+ tumor and very young age at diagnosis are the major factors associated with a significantly increased risk of breast recurrence; (2) the risk of breast relapse is not significantly influenced by tumor size, histologic grade, lymph node status, or the presence of a margin of normal tissue around the primary tumor.
